archetype.name: Pocket Passer (sack-averse)
archetype.definition: A veteran rhythm thrower who wins from the pocket by getting the ball out on time to the 10-to-19-yard level, rarely takes sacks, and adds only scramble yardage with his legs.

report.headline: Shootout volume and a clean pocket keep him top-tier while his accuracy slips
report.take:
Prescott in his 11th season is what he has mostly been: a pocket quarterback who lives on timing throws outside the numbers and in the intermediate zone, with enough mobility to escape rather than to run. His time to throw (2.81) and aggressiveness (19.38%) are almost identical to last year's 2.82 and 20.3, so the operation has not changed. What has changed is the context. Dallas has the worst defense in the league by EPA (32nd of 32), so he keeps dropping back to chase points. That is why he ranks 3rd in passing yards and 3rd in TDs while his efficiency sits closer to 11th in EPA per dropback.

The passing game is built on the left side and the 10-plus air-yard throws. His 132 attempts of 10+ air yards average 0.371 EPA and account for more value than his 255 short ones. Throws to the left are worth 0.294 EPA, against 0.052 over the middle, where three of his six interceptions came. Pickens (0.328 EPA per target) and Flournoy (0.347) have been more efficient per look than Lamb, though Lamb's 123 targets still produce the most total value. The protection piece is the quiet star: a 3.7% sack rate (3rd) and a 16.3% pressure-to-sack rate (3rd) are the best of his career. Past seasons ran anywhere from 19% to 35%, so this is a real change, helped by a line that ranks 9th in hit rate allowed.

Two things in the numbers are softer than they look. First, accuracy. His CPOE is down 1.7 points from last year and his bad-throw rate is up 2.8 points to 14% (21st), after he sat 6th last season. Over the last three games his CPOE is -2.6 even as the TDs piled up. Second, game state. He has been better trailing by 9+ (0.224 EPA, 112 plays) than within one score (0.102). Some of the efficiency is catch-up work against defenses sitting back. Third down (-0.031 EPA) is mediocre, and the 16 red-zone TDs came on 49.2% completions, a TD haul that should cool.

The outlook still favors volume. His defense is not going to suddenly stop people, the offense ranks 5th in EPA, and the receivers are winning. Two threats sit on the horizon. The protection that has carried his sack avoidance just lost a 94%-snap guard. And the sack rate had already climbed to 6.6% over the last three games. If the ball keeps coming out on time, he stays a top-five fantasy quarterback on volume alone. If the line leaks, the slipping accuracy has less margin to hide behind.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep efficiency
strengths.body: His 10-to-19-yard throws return 0.36 EPA with 8 TDs, and his deep shots 0.395, even with 35.7% completions there. That is the outside-the-numbers game with Pickens and Lamb working, and it has been a staple across his best seasons. It should hold as long as protection gives him time to hit the drop.

strengths.title: Career-best sack avoidance
strengths.body: A 3.7% sack rate and 16.3% pressure-to-sack rate both rank 3rd. His time to throw is unchanged, so this comes from processing plus a line that ranks 9th in hit rate allowed, not from dumping the ball early. It is the most fragile strength on the list. It rests partly on personnel, and the last three games already show more sacks.

strengths.title: Volume locked in by his defense
strengths.body: Dallas ranks 32nd in defensive EPA, so he is throwing 38.7 times a game and pacing for 4,631 yards. That keeps a high floor for yards and TDs regardless of efficiency swings. It lasts as long as the defense stays bottom-tier, which nothing in the dossier suggests will change.

concerns.title: Accuracy has slipped from last year
concerns.body: His CPOE is down 1.7 points and his bad-throw rate is up 2.8 points from a 2025 season in which he ranked 6th in bad throws. The last three games show a -2.6 CPOE. The time to throw and aggressiveness are unchanged, so this is not a scheme shift. It looks like plain ball placement, similar to his weaker 2024. Explosive plays are covering for it for now.

concerns.title: Middle of the field and third down
concerns.body: Throws over the middle produce just 0.052 EPA with a -5.6 CPOE and 3 interceptions. Third down sits slightly negative at -0.031 EPA. Both point to tight-window throws being the weak link, and losing Ferguson removes his main inside target for now.

concerns.title: Protection losing its starting guard
concerns.body: Tyler Booker (94% of snaps) is out with a high-ankle sprain, with a return estimated around December 7. The sack rate had already risen to 6.6% over the last three games. A weaker interior is the most direct threat to the clean pocket his game depends on.

trend.note: Outside a two-game dip against Tampa Bay and Green Bay (both top-10 defenses now), he has posted positive passing EPA every week, and the last three games run slightly above his season efficiency. The TD spike over that stretch came with worse accuracy and more sacks.

nextGame.headline: Titans' leaky pass defense sets up another big volume day
nextGame.body:
Tennessee is about as soft a matchup as his profile could ask for. The Titans rank 30th in pass EPA allowed, last in explosive pass rate, and last in passing yards allowed to quarterbacks. Opposing WR1s have run well above their norms against them, which points straight at Lamb. Teams tend to run on Tennessee more than usual, but that reflects a respectable run defense rather than strength in coverage. The caveat is script. Dallas is a big favorite and Tennessee's offense ranks 26th in EPA, so this may not become the shootout his defense usually forces. A comfortable lead could cap his attempts late, and he has rarely played with big leads this year.

Availability cuts both ways. Tennessee is without both regular linebackers, including the 100%-snap Anthony Hill Jr. That softens the middle of the field, where he has struggled most. Safety Tony Adams is also questionable after a concussion. On his side, Booker's absence at guard matters most, and Ferguson's knee removes his tight end. That narrows the passing game further toward Lamb, Pickens and Flournoy. The roof is retractable and the early forecast is mild, so weather is not a factor.

keyMatchups.title: Lamb against a WR1 sieve
keyMatchups.body: Tennessee allows 0.55 EPA per target to opposing WR1s (30th), and those receivers have beaten their usual output by a wide margin. Lamb leads the team with 123 targets, so this is where the volume should go. Five-plus games is still a modest sample, but it fits the Titans' overall pass-defense rankings.

keyMatchups.title: Explosive plays downfield
keyMatchups.body: The Titans give up the most explosive passes in the league. His 10+ air-yard game is the engine of his efficiency, which makes this the clearest edge on the board.

keyMatchups.title: Game script as the cap
keyMatchups.body: With Dallas favored by 8.5 against an offense ranked 26th, a lead could pull him off the throttle. He has played only 18 snaps leading by 9+ this season, so this is unfamiliar territory for his usage.

nextGame.watch: How the interior line holds up without Booker: if the sack rate stays in last-three-game territory, the efficiency edge shrinks even in a soft matchup.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is the safest thing here. A last-ranked defense and a top-five offense mean 35-40 attempts a week, with yards near his 272-per-game season rate. The intermediate and deep efficiency, and the targets producing it, have held up across his career. The TD rate is the piece to fade a little. Sixteen red-zone TDs on sub-50% red-zone completions, plus a recent stretch of high TD rate alongside a negative CPOE, are more likely to cool than to repeat. I'd project 1.7 to 2.3 TDs a game rather than the recent 2.67.

The sack avoidance is the swing factor. It is a career outlier, and with Booker out into December the most likely direction is modest regression toward his past norms. The accuracy dip looks real given the bad-throw trend. It is not severe enough to sink him while the offense creates this many explosives, but it lowers his floor in games against stronger coverage units, like the Tampa Bay and Green Bay weeks.
swingFactors: Whether ball placement rebounds toward 2025 levels
Dallas defense forcing shootouts versus protecting leads

confidence.note: Ten starts and a stable career profile, but protection and target personnel are changing.
